note: TWO OF THESE FIGURES ARE GATED AND TWO ARE NOT, and which is which is a measurement rather than a preference. This study is one of six taken on the same commit across five processors of the runner pool. Wall clock TTI came out between 163.7 and 216.1 ms over those six, a range of 25.7 percent of the median, and total main thread task time, which was proposed as the machine independent replacement for it, came out at 27.0 percent, so SPEC 20 records both and gates neither. What did not move is the count of tasks over 50 ms, which read 2 as the median of 25 navigations on every one of the six, and the three byte columns, which were identical to the byte on all of them. Those two carry the thresholds. The runner CPU is not fixed within one image, so re-recording this file against a study taken on another processor compares nothing: the ceilings would still be checked and the relative TTI line would be meaningless.
